summary.intent: Land a fix so the npm dependency parser reads v-prefixed and ~> specs as their plain forms, open a PR for it, and then address a CI failure on another PR (#541) where a new empty-entry rejection broke an existing test.
summary.outcome: Committed (signed) and pushed fix/npm-v-prefixed-specs, and PR #545 was updated with title/body and marked ready. For #541, the CI failure was traced to the empty-entry rejection for artifact targets and edits were made to cli.rs and the changeset on fix/init-artifact-target-trim; a local check script was run, but its result isn't shown in the transcript.

repo: Only one known test in registry-tools fails locally and in CI; CI skips it, so local checks should judge exit codes while skipping that test.
Trails are linked to PRs via `entire trail link <id> --repo ... --project ... --branch ... --base main`.
Changes to behavior in callisto-cli are accompanied by a changeset file in .changeset/ (e.g. init-artifact-target-trims-spaces.md).

The artifact-target flag handling lives in crates/callisto-cli/src/cli.rs (artifact_target_flag_splits_on_comma test and trimmed_triple helper); rejecting empty entries with 'a target triple cannot be empty' conflicts with existing tests.

code.finding: The trimmed_triple function and artifact_target_flag_splits_on_comma test interact: the new empty-entry rejection broke the existing test, so the function or the test was adjusted on fix/init-artifact-target-trim.

workflow: Use `gh run view <run-id> --log-failed` with grep filters to pull out failing tests quickly from CI logs.
Fetch and inspect the other branch's version of a file with `git show origin/<branch>:<path>` before switching to it.
Work happens in a git worktree (.claude/worktrees/verify-manifest-findings), so confirm the current branch with `git branch --show-current` before editing.
Keep PR bodies in a temp file and apply with `gh pr edit --body-file` then `gh pr ready`.
